messages:
inc-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate detected for tenant harbinger on dedicated-cluster-us-east-2 · 5m error rate = 18% (> 2% threshold) :rotating_light: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/4981234567
Priya (oncall): ack — paging Dylan for infra/eviction look. Priya (oncall) taking lead for now.
Dylan R: on it, joining. can someone paste the query for 5xx by route?
Priya (oncall): grafana -> /dashboards/dedicated/tenant-overview -> filter harbinger. 5xx spike started ~09:12 UTC, p95 latency jumped to 3.2s, inflight queue per-router ~240 (normal 30).
Kai: seeing concurrent streams for harbinger storming to many long-running streams, KV eviction spikes on the dedicated nodes (evictions/s ~1200). logs show repeated `kv: miss -> fetch` churn.
Dylan R: running quick checks — `kubectl top pods -n dedicated-harbinger` shows two router pods at 98% CPU, kv-store pod OOMKilled recently and restarted once.
Dylan R: log tail (router):
```
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z router-1 ERROR gateway: upstream 502 "connection reset" for req tenant=harbinger model=qa-v2 seq=...
2026-03-15T09:13:04Z router-1 WARN cache: evict key=prefix/abcd count=1 reason=capacity
2026-03-15T09:13:11Z router-2 ERROR timeout: request ctx deadline exceeded tenant=harbinger
```
Priya (oncall): looks like a KV thrash + router saturation -> downstream 502/504s and timeouts. likely noisy-tenant behaviour (sudden high concurrency + long context).
Evan: adding infra context — dedicated-cluster-us-east-2 has 6 worker nodes reserved for dedicated pools; utilisation at the time: 94%. We can spin up 2 warm nodes from pool-burst (will take ~3-4m).
Dylan R: mitigation options: 1) enable per-tenant concurrency cap for harbinger (soft cap 40) 2) temporarily route new harbinger requests to the hosted fallback model (lower capacity pressure) 3) increase pool size + restart kv pod to clear eviction loops. I can apply 1 and 2 now.
Priya (oncall): do 1 + 2, notify CS. Kai, can you confirm if evictions correlate with specific prefix/large cache keys?
Kai: yes — evictions concentrated on `prefix/session-*` keys. harbinger has long-lived conversation state with many distinct prefixes per user. evictions spike coincides with many simultaneous cold-start requests.
Dylan R: applying tenant concurrency cap -> `redwoodctl tenants update harbinger --max-concurrency 40 --reason "auto-mitigation noisy tenant"`
Dylan R: routing new requests to hosted fallback: `routes apply --tenant harbinger --fallback hosted-small-v1 --weight 100` (applied).
Priya (oncall): deploying change now. will monitor 60s windows.
(1 min later)
Dylan R: metrics update: 5xx dropped from 18% -> 6% in 60s; p95 latency down to 1.1s, inflight queue ~70. still some tail errors.
Jaime (CS): pinging HarbingerOps via email/slack to let them know we're throttling concurrency and routing to fallback. offering to open a support window. any customer-visible error pages yet?
Priya (oncall): customer-facing endpoints returned 502 for some requests during peak — CS reach-out in progress. no broad data loss; errors are transient and tied to capacity.
Evan: I've started 2 warm nodes from pool-burst; ETA ~3m. once up, we can revert routing and remove cap if safe.
Dylan R: also cleaning KV cache loop — restarting kv pod to clear fragmentation: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/kv-harbinger -n dedicated-harbinger` (restarted).
(3 min later)
Kai: kv pod restart succeeded, eviction rate dropped ~80%. router CPU normalized to ~60% after new nodes came up.
Priya (oncall): 5xx now at 1.2% and trending down, p95 0.48s. rolling back fallback to hosted? or keep for 10m to be safe.
Dylan R: recommend keep fallback for 10m, keep cap for 15m, then gradually remove. I'll own a gradual rollback and handoff.
Priya (oncall): assigning follow-up to Dylan for postmortem and cleanup. Dylan -> please include request patterns, long-lived conversation analysis, and recommended per-tenant limits in the PM.
Dylan R: ack. taking postmortem.
Jaime (CS): updated HarbingerOps: we limited concurrency + routed to fallback while autoscale + node additions mitigated the issue; they acknowledged and asked for daily summary.
Priya (oncall): summary for ops log: 2026-03-15 09:12 UTC — surge in long-lived concurrent requests from Harbinger caused KV thrash and router saturation -> elevated 5xx/timeouts. Mitigations: tenant concurrency cap, route to hosted fallback, restarted kv pod, added 2 warm nodes. Result: 5xx reduced to ~1.2% within 6m; customer notified.
Kai: suggestion for prevention: add per-tenant proactive autoscaling trigger on KV eviction rate and add quota guardrails for long-lived sessions.
Dylan R: handoff note -> I'll keep an eye for 30m, then postmortem with timeline + suggested config changes. tagging infra for any capacity adjustments later.
Priya (oncall): thanks team. marking as incident-resolved for immediate customer impact. will attach graphs and logs to ticket #INC-2026-4981. :white_check_mark:
